title: "Cleaning log"

::: {.simulated}
**Simulated data — not real patients.** FLUID-ICU is an invented study: every value was produced by a computer program with a fixed random seed. It does not describe any real patient, hospital or ICU. Any manuscript written from it must say that the data are simulated and must never be submitted as real research.
:::

> **SIMULATED DATA - NOT REAL PATIENTS.** This log belongs to the teaching dataset FLUID-ICU.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Raw file** | `fluid_icu_raw.csv` (identical content in `fluid_icu_raw.xlsx`): 623 rows, 29 columns, as received from ICU A-D |
| **Clean file** | `fluid_icu_clean.csv` / `.rds`: 620 patients, 32 variables |
| **Cleaning script** | `R/01_clean.R` (each step below is one block of the script) |
| **Check** | The script rebuilds the clean file from the raw file and confirms it is identical, value for value and byte for byte |
| **Rule** | The raw file is never edited. Every change is made by the script and written down here. |

## Problems found and what we did

| Step | Problem found | How many | What we did | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Column names typed like a spreadsheet: spaces, brackets, capitals (`Weight (kg)`, `MAP (mmHg)`, `VFD 28`) | 29 columns | Converted to short lower-case names with `clean_names()`; renamed 4 (e.g. `map_mm_hg` to `map_mmhg`, `vfd_28` to `vent_free_days_28`) | Names without spaces are easy to type and the same in every script |
| 2 | Duplicate records: the same patient entered twice | 3 IDs (FLU-139, FLU-274, FLU-574): 623 rows for 620 patients | Checked that the two copies were identical in every column, then kept one copy | Each patient must be counted once |
| 3 | ICU name typed in different ways (`icu a`, `ICU-A`, `ICUA`, trailing space) | 14 rows | Standardised to `ICU A`, `ICU B`, `ICU C`, `ICU D` | Otherwise R sees 11 "different" ICUs |
| 4 | Admission date in three formats: `2023-03-14`, `14/03/2023`, `14-Mar-2023` | 365 / 164 / 94 rows | Read each format explicitly and converted all to one date (YYYY-MM-DD); 0 dates failed | Mixed formats are read wrongly or not at all; 03/04 could be March or April |
| 5 | Sex coded 9 ways (`Male`, `M`, `m`, `male`, `Female`, `F`, `f`, `female`, ` Female`) | 200 rows not `Male`/`Female` | Recoded to `Female` / `Male` | One variable, one coding |
| 6 | Yes/No variables mixed `Yes`, `No`, `Y`, `N`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, `0` (ICU B sends 1/0) | 8 variables; about 1,900 cells not `Yes`/`No` | Recoded to `No` / `Yes`; checked that no value was lost | `1` and `Yes` must mean the same thing |
| 7 | All columns read as text | all | Converted numbers to numbers (whole numbers as integers) | Needed for calculations |
| 8 | Missing-value codes used as if they were numbers: lactate `999` and `-99`, APACHE II `-99`, MAP `999` | Lactate 21 (12 x 999, 9 x -99), APACHE II 6, MAP 4 | Set to missing (`NA`) | A lactate of 999 would wreck the mean; missing is missing |
| 9 | Units: ICU C reported lactate in **mg/dL**, the other ICUs in mmol/L (ICU C median 23.8 vs about 2.5 elsewhere) | 126 values (all ICU C lactates) | Divided ICU C values by 9.01 (1 mmol/L = 9.01 mg/dL), 1 decimal; ICU C median became 2.65 | One unit for one variable; found by comparing medians by ICU |
| 10 | Impossible values (outside the allowed range in the data dictionary) | 3: FLU-529 age 210; FLU-277 weight 7 kg; FLU-282 day-2 output -2990 ml | Set to missing and raised a query with the site. The patient stays in the study | We cannot guess the true value (21? 71?); deleting the patient would bias the sample |
| 10b | Range checks on all other variables (SOFA, APACHE II, lactate, MAP, AKI stage, VFD, ICU stay, follow-up time; survivors followed to day 28) | 0 problems | None | Documents that the checks were done |
| 11 | Infection source as free text | 5 categories | Fixed category order (Respiratory, Urinary, Abdominal, Skin/soft tissue, Other) | Same order in every table |
| 12 | Derived variables needed (not in the raw file) | 3 new variables | Computed `cum_fluid_balance_d3_ml_kg` = (fluid in d1-3 - fluid out d1-3) / weight; `positive_balance_d3` (> 0 ml/kg); `aki_any` (KDIGO stage >= 1) | Derived values are calculated by the script, never typed by hand |

## Missing data after cleaning (real missing values, reported in the papers)

| Variable | Missing | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `lactate_mmol_l` | 93 (15.0%) | Not measured (more often in less severe patients and in ICU D) |
| `apache_ii` | 6 (1.0%) | Not recorded |
| `map_mmhg` | 4 (0.6%) | Not recorded |
| `age` | 1 | Impossible value set to missing (query pending) |
| `weight_kg` | 1 | Impossible value set to missing (query pending) |
| `fluid_out_d2_ml` | 1 | Impossible value set to missing (query pending) |
| `cum_fluid_balance_d3_ml_kg`, `positive_balance_d3` | 2 | Follows from the missing weight and output above |

## Queries sent to sites (simulated)

| Query | Patient | Variable | Value in raw file | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q-001 | FLU-529 (ICU B) | Age | 210 | Open - set to missing |
| Q-002 | FLU-277 (ICU C) | Weight | 7 kg | Open - set to missing |
| Q-003 | FLU-282 (ICU A) | Fluid out, day 2 | -2990 ml | Open - set to missing |
| Q-004 | ICU C | Lactate unit | mg/dL | Confirmed by site lab - converted |

*Teaching note:* in a real study the site would correct the source record and the database, and the cleaning script would be re-run. Here the queries stay open so that the clean file is fixed for the course.
